jobs.title: Senior Director, Commercial Finance & Performance Management (CFPM)
jobs.description:
Company:

Finning International Inc.

Number of Openings:

1

Worker Type:

Permanent

Position Overview:

Finning Canada is hiring a Permanent, Full-time Senior Director, Commercial Finance & Performance Management (CFPM), based in either Edmonton or Calgary.

Reporting to the Vice President, Finance & Supply Chain, this role represents one of the most senior and influential finance leadership positions within Finning Canada. As the senior commercial finance leader for a ~$6B revenue business, the Senior Director, CFPM plays a pivotal role in driving profitable growth, optimizing capital deployment, and strengthening commercial governance across the organization. Partnering closely with Canadian Operations, this leader oversees the Commercial & Financial Business Partnering team and serves as a trusted advisor to senior and executive leadership, translating strategy into actionable financial insight.

Leading a high-performing team of finance leaders, the role champions strong commercial acumen, best-in-class budgeting, forecasting, and strategic planning, and delivers insightful financial and operational reporting to enable data-driven decision-making and effective performance management. With significant exposure to the Canadian leadership team and the broader Finning Executive, this role offers the opportunity to lead high-impact initiatives, influence enterprise-wide strategy, and shape the financial future of the business. Positioned as a key succession role to the VP, Finance & Supply Chain, this role provides a clear pathway to broader executive accountability and long-term leadership growth within Finning.

Job Description:

Major Job Functions:

Strategic & Commercial Leadership

Drive financial strategy aligned to Finning and Caterpillar objectives
Provide executive decision support and investment governance
Identify competitive trends and growth opportunities
Operate with integrity through maintaining social, ethical and organizational integrity in conducting business activities; maintains confidentiality, adheres to corporate policies and procedures
Accountable for the Commercial Governance for Finning Canada. $6Bn+ of revenue, $500M of EBIT
Accountable for delivering the strategic plan, governance processes and alignment internally with Finning and Caterpillar
Accountable to be a change agent in how we manage and re-shape the business

Drive Financial Performance across the business

Leader in driving, understanding and analysing financial performance on a monthly, quarterly and annual basis
Owner of identifying gaps in performance and implementing action plans to address
Take an objective view, balancing operational and corporate requirements
Identify, communicate, and mitigate potential issues or liabilities; recommend effective solutions
Focus on EBIT, Invested Capital, ROIC and FCF

Financial Planning, Analysis & Reporting

Own budgeting, forecasting, and long‑range plans
Responsible for the efficient management of financial and accounting operations including financial reporting, budgeting, asset management and control
Provide financially sound information and manage the effective flow of that information through financial systems, reports, and dashboards
Ensure high‑quality C‑suite reporting and KPI insight
Improve forecast accuracy and performance analytics

Governance & Capital Discipline

Lead large deal/tender governance and post‑investment review
Approve major commercial decisions and business cases

Leadership & Stakeholder Influence

Act as trusted advisor to the FINCA EC, FLT, and Board
Represent FINCA with Caterpillar and external stakeholders
Lead the CFPM Team, driving engagement, development talent and providing a succession pipeline
100% accountability for results and impact on people by setting a strong example in high performance leadership

Education and Qualifications:

10+ years of relevant industry experience is required
10+ years experience in a leadership capacity
10+ years of progressive accounting experience in related industry or public practice.
Master's or Bachelor’s degree in finance or related degree preferred
Accounting designation or graduate degree preferred
Highly effective senior leadership skills gained through previous leadership experience
Experience leading implementation projects for financial systems at a senior leader level, on a global scale (system examples: BPC, SAP, Hyperion, M3, Peoplesoft, or Other)
Practical experience and theoretical knowledge in Dealership Business Models, end-to-end supply chain management and Financial & Commercial practices
Operational experience across a number of disciplines / functions
Global business strategy and corporate finance knowledge
Advanced general accounting knowledge coupled with a sound understanding of business processes, the interrelationship of business functions, corporate governance issues and operational needs
Knowledge of financial systems with historical proven, positive track record of solution implementation, optimization, and sustainment
Knowledge of the operations of related industry segments
Proficient in the use of MS Office Suite and in-house systems including BPC, M3, Power BI, Concur
Understands and adheres to Finning policies and procedures, including safety, inclusion, and diversity
Ability to determine key performance indicators (KPIs), variance issues and improve internal controls
Experience working with CAT systems, tools, data, or reports including DFRS, CAT dealer portal is preferred
Change management training, experience, and/or PROSCI or Lean Change Agent certification preferred

Soft Skills:

Strong team leadership skills, capable of representing the business at a senior management level with robust stakeholder management.
Effective verbal communication skills, presenting messages clearly, concisely, and directly.
Influencing skills, ability to drive results without direct line responsibility and ensure the wider team are engaged and effective.
Strong Analytical / Problem solving attributes. Ability to Design, interrogate and review Financial and Operational information and create clear and effective understanding with stakeholders.
Advanced Commercial acumen with the ability to drive improvements in financial returns and profitability.
Ability to clearly articulate the value of financial analysis, linked to business results
Must possess highest standard of accuracy and precision and be highly organized
Self motivated and results oriented, with a desire to achieve
Ability to deal with ambiguity and assist in creating sustainable competitive advantage
Effective change management capabilities
Professional, timely and accurate presentation of information
Ability to continuously learn and develop role related skills
Ability to manage, motivate and develop a large and diverse team

At Finning, we prioritize creating a diverse and inclusive environment. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and we actively encourage all individuals to express themselves and achieve their full potential. As a company, we continuously strive to enhance our outreach to individuals of all backgrounds and identities. We do not discriminate against applicants based on gender identity, race, national and ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, marital and family status, and/or mental or physical disabilities. Furthermore, Finning is committed to collaborating with and providing reasonable accommodations /adjustments to individuals with disabilities. If you require an adjustment/accommodation at any point during the recruitment process, please inform your recruiter.

jobs.title: Director, Strategy & Operations
jobs.description:
Role Summary

The Director, Strategy & Operations is a high-impact role supporting senior leadership. The team supports strategy development and value creation through major strategic initiatives across asset and wealth management.

This position blends strategy, corporate development, M&A, and transformation, with significant exposure to senior leadership and key business priorities.

Key Responsibilities

Conduct analysis and develop frameworks to address key strategic questions and inform business priorities, including product positioning and growth opportunities.
Conduct due diligence on potential acquisitions and partnership opportunities.
Support integration and execution planning for completed transactions.
Lead and execute major transformation initiatives, improving decision-making and accelerating delivery.
Manage external partners, including investment banks, consultants, and technology vendors.
Prepare executive-ready materials to support rigorous decision-making on critical business issues for senior leadership and the board.

Qualifications

4+ years of experience in management consulting, corporate strategy, corporate development/M&A, or investment banking, ideally with exposure to asset or wealth management.
Ability to operate as a strategic thought partner to senior executives, including framing ambiguous problems and developing actionable recommendations.
Strong M&A and financial modeling skills, including valuation, deal structuring, due diligence, and integration.
Experience leading or contributing to cross-functional transformation and change initiatives within complex organizations.
Excellent communication skills with the ability to translate complex strategic and financial information into clear, executive-ready materials.
Strong analytical skills and the ability to synthesize large amounts of information into structured insights and frameworks.

Compensation: The base salary range for this position is $165,000–$185,000 CAD annually.

Location: This is an onsite position in downtown Toronto, conveniently located near Union Station.

jobs.title: Leader, LCR Strategy and Operations
jobs.description:
Who We Are:

Every transaction matters. Every Canadian matters. At Interac, we protect both — driving trust, security, and inclusion, so our digital economy thrives.

Founded in 1984, Interac connects Canadians through secure digital payments, advanced identity verification and industry-leading fraud protection. Connecting banks, businesses, and individuals, Interac enables millions to send, receive, and manage money safely and effortlessly every day — across both digital and physical environments.

As the backbone of Canada’s financial ecosystem, Interac facilitates over 20 million transactions daily, supported by trusted partnerships with government and financial institutions. Consistently ranked as Canada’s most reputable financial technology brand, Interac is deeply embedded in the daily lives of Canadians.

Who You Will Work With:

The vacant Leader, LCR Strategy and Operations role will report to the Group Head, General Counsel and will work collaboratively with a close-knit team of sharp, solution-oriented lawyers, auditors and compliance professionals to oversee and advance departmental operations.

You will oversee the strategic execution of the legal, internal audit and compliance team’s operations at Canada’s domestic debit card network, all the while gaining exposure to dynamic areas of legal, internal audit and compliance within the financial services and FinTech environment. This role combines legal operations expertise with strong people leadership to ensure alignment with organizational goals and continuous team development. You will have the ability to shape key operational improvement initiatives that enable the business and will be responsible for designing processes and systems to ensure efficient performance of the team.

We are looking for a self-motivated, innovative, and responsible team player and leader, with demonstrated maturity, sound judgement and professionalism who can lead strategic and operational planning processes for the team, including a 3-year strategy, annual business planning, objective setting and tracking, and a team technology strategy. In addition, the Leader will provide strategic guidance and support to the leadership team and play a central role in managing the day-to-day operations of the LCR team, including financial management, technology management and strategy, LCR vendor management, knowledge management, business and operational planning. The LCR Strategy and Operations Leader will be a leader, facilitator and enabler of key projects, communications, reports and other activities that support the mandate of the LCR team. Interac requires someone with exceptional organizational and interpersonal skills.

What You Will Do:

Develop the team’s strategy and annual work plans to formalize the build out of the operational function in the team and ensuring achievement of milestones and objectives
Partner with IT and Vendor Management teams to develop and achieve a technology strategy and successfully implementing and managing technology solutions, including document management, contract lifecycle management, various tools, applications, licenses and subscriptions
Support the leadership team in developing and maintaining a talent strategy, including recruitment, retention, on-boarding/off-boarding, new hire training, resource allocation employee engagement and organizing team-building events and meetings
Ensure both the team’s and organization’s EDI goals are built into talent sourcing and pipeline strategies
Drive and support team operational excellence, conduct research and provide education to the leadership team on best practices to improve overall operational effectiveness
Optimize operational effectiveness by identifying opportunities for greater efficiency and implementing practices, tools and technology to improve workflows and processes
Lead strategic and operational planning processes for the team, including annual business planning, objective-setting and developing the team’s technology strategy
Create data and metrics to enhance reporting capabilities that demonstrate value, measure progress and provide insights into opportunities for improved effectiveness, and better-informed decision-making
Oversee project planning to ensure successful implementation of team-sponsored projects through effective management of stakeholders, timelines, budgets and resources
Successfully collaborate and align with business partners on cross-functional initiatives and provide required team responses on organization-wide initiatives such as cost reporting, business continuity planning and coordination of responses to internal and external auditing requests.
Design and implement processes and procedures to improve workflow management, create efficiencies and advance departmental strategies
Facilitate training and enablement sessions for team members to ensure effective adoption of new technology and processes
Develop the legal team’s external counsel program and manage and maintain successful team vendor relationships
Develop team knowledge management practices and facilitate organization-wide training on legal topics and/or legal processes and procedures
Oversee team information and data governance and record management practices including any litigation hold practices
Ensure a consistent and efficient approach to the delivery of legal, compliance and audit services across the organization and making recommendations to the leadership team on continuous improvement opportunities
Craft clear, concise, articulate and timely communications and materials (including presentation decks) with an appropriate level of detail
Maintain visibility into team performance, engagement, and workload
Effectively delegate tasks across the team
Conduct one-on-one meetings and team check-ins to foster open communication
Identify skill gaps, coordinate training, and support career progression
Keep a pulse on individual career aspirations and integrate them into development plans
Lead performance reviews, provide feedback, and ensure transparent evaluation processes
Address and escalate challenges impacting team well-being or delivery
Review proposed OKRs, lead annual planning sessions, and align team goals with organizational priorities

What You Bring:

You have an undergraduate degree and a minimum 7 years’ related experience in legal operations
You have knowledge and understanding of departmental operations and related competencies (financial, human resource management, business development, records management, technology, information governance, vendor management, data analytics, and knowledge management)
You have experience in strategic planning, design, and facilitation
Proven leader with strong people management experience
Preferably, you have experience in business management, project management, change management and process development
Preferably, you have knowledge and understanding of the legal industry and corporate legal departments systems, processes, procedures and best practices
You are a process-oriented self-starter with a continuous improvement mindset who stays informed on best practices in operational management and technology developments
You are results-oriented with demonstrated abilities in operational excellence and working both independently and collaboratively to move projects forward
You have excellent verbal and written communication skills, including presentation and training/education skills
You are a highly collaborative, relationship-builder with strong interpersonal skills with the ability to develop trust and confidence, work effectively and collaborative with individuals across multiple functions and levels
You can comfortably manage and prioritize workloads in a fast-paced environment that is continuously evolving
You have strong organizational and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic, fast-paced, deadline-oriented environment
You are meticulous, diligent, and attentive to details with the ability to produce high quality work under pressure
You are technologically savvy with the ability to leverage technological tools to enhance process efficiency and build reports as necessary, proficient with Microsoft Office Suite (Outlook, Word, Power Point, Excel, Power BI, MS Teams)
You can independently manage competing priorities with sensitivity to internal stakeholders and deadlines
You have demonstrated maturity, sound judgement and discretion and an ability to maintain the confidentiality of sensitive material and information
You have a proven ability to solve problems independently and a willingness to tackle new challenges and upgrade skills when required
You have strong meeting/event planning skills and an ability to lead virtual and in-person meetings

What We’re Offering:

The hiring range for this position is $140,000 to $160,000, and you will also be eligible for our short-term incentive plan. The exact amount will depend on factors such as skills, experience, and job-related knowledge, but Interac’s commitment goes beyond compensation. Our Total Rewards package is designed to support your well-being and future, and includes:

Generous vacation and wellness days to help you recharge
Comprehensive employer-paid benefits coverage for peace of mind
Market-leading employer-funded RRSP program to invest in your future
Flexible hybrid work model for better work-life balance
Access to a free and confidential 24/7 employee & family assistance program to offer support for you and your immediate family
Pregnancy and parental leave top-up to support growing families
Charitable donation matching with United Way to amplify your impact

Why Join Us?

At Interac, the impact we make, and the people who drive it, is profound. When you become part of our team, you’re joining a purpose-driven organization that’s shaping the future of digital finance in Canada. Here’s what you can expect:

Investing in the Future – Help us unlock digital prosperity for all Canadians.
Innovative Thinking – Collaborate on products, practices, and platforms that redefine what’s possible.
Inclusive Culture – Be empowered to bring your whole self to work and realize your full potential.
Inspiring Community – Work in an ecosystem where we lift each other up and rise together.
Intentional Support – Enjoy flexible, supportive offerings that prioritize your total wellness.

Additional Pre-Employment Requirements:

To ensure the integrity of our organization, successful candidates will be required to complete background checks, which may include, Canadian Criminal Credit Check, Canadian ID Cross-Check, Public Safety Verification, 5-year Employment Verification, Education Verification, Credit Check, and Social Media Check.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Interac is also an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. We believe that innovation thrives when people from different backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives come together. That’s why we are committed to providing fair and equitable employment opportunities for all individuals, without discrimination based on race, color, ancestry, ethnic origin, place of origin, citizenship, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, marital or family status, disability, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

If you require accommodation during any stage of the application or recruitment process, please contact us at humanresources@interac.ca. We will work with you to meet your needs.

Please be aware that certain individuals are misusing Interac Corp.’s name and logo to promote fictitious employment opportunities. Interac Corp. never requests, solicits, or accepts any form of payment in exchange for employment. Any such offers are fraudulent and should be disregarded. jobs.title: Finance Director
jobs.description:
Permanent

Job title:

Group Finance Director
Salary:

$180,000 - $190,000 + Bonus
Role status:

Current opening
Our client:

A well-established North American manufacturing organization with operations across Canada and the U.S.
Principal tasks and responsibilities include:

Provide overall leadership and direction to the Finance function across the organization.

Lead, coach, develop, and motivate the Finance team while building a positive, collaborative, and accountable culture.

Build strong relationships across Finance and the broader business, creating an environment where people feel supported, heard, and valued.

Act as a trusted Finance business partner to senior leadership and operational stakeholders.

Work closely with plant operations, supply chain, and other functional leaders to understand business priorities and provide financial insight and recommendations.

Build strong relationships with operational leaders and understand the business behind the numbers.

Listen to business stakeholders, understand their challenges, and translate financial information into practical business recommendations.

Work collaboratively with leaders across the organization to identify opportunities, solve problems, and support business objectives.

Challenge the business constructively while maintaining strong relationships, credibility, and trust.

Provide leadership with clear financial insight to support strategic and operational decision-making.

Lead monthly, quarterly, and year-end financial close and reporting processes for Canadian and U.S. entities.

Oversee consolidated reporting, balance sheet reviews, and preparation of financial statements.

Lead budgeting, forecasting, cash flow planning, and financial performance reporting.

Oversee external audit processes and act as a key liaison with external auditors.

Provide oversight of tax, treasury, banking, intercompany, and financial control activities.

Provide financial oversight and guidance related to inventory, costing, operational spending, and business performance.

Identify opportunities to improve Finance processes, reporting, controls, and overall effectiveness.

Partner with senior leadership on business initiatives, investments, operational decisions, and broader organizational priorities.

Ensure the Finance function is aligned with the organization's strategic objectives and provides meaningful value to the business.

Qualifications and pre-requisites:

· CPA designation
· Significant progressive Finance leadership experience
· Proven experience leading, coaching, and developing Finance teams
· Strong Canadian and U.S. Finance experience
· Strong technical knowledge across financial reporting, forecasting, budgeting, cash flow, month-end, and year-end close
· Experience with financial controls and external audit processes
· Manufacturing or automotive industry experience strongly preferred
· Demonstrated business partnering experience with senior leadership and operational stakeholders
· Strong business and commercial acumen with the ability to understand operational priorities and connect them to financial performance
· Strong ERP and financial systems experience, along with advanced Excel skills
· Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
· Strong listening skills with the ability to understand different perspectives and build trust across an organization
· Demonstrated emotional intelligence, maturity, and professionalism as a people leader
· Proven ability to build strong, collaborative relationships across different functions and levels of an organization
· Ability to navigate differing opinions and challenging situations in a constructive and professional manner
· Collaborative leadership style with the ability to influence, challenge, and bring people together
· Strong judgment and ability to balance technical Finance requirements with broader business objectives
· Ability to operate effectively in a complex, fast-paced environment with multiple competing priorities
Additional information or perks:

Full-time, permanent position

Onsite position in Windsor, Ontario

$180,000 - $190,000 base salary plus bonus

Highly confidential Group-level search

Due to the confidential nature of this search, candidates and third parties must not communicate with or contact employees regarding this opportunity.

The search is being conducted confidentially on behalf of the Group and will be charged at the Group level.

With significant exposure to the Canadian leadership team and the broader Finning Executive, this role offers the opportunity to lead high-impact initiatives, influence enterprise-wide strategy, and shape the financial future of the business. Positioned as a key succession role to the VP, Finance & Supply Chain, this role provides a clear pathway to broader executive accountability and long-term leadership growth within Finning.
